title: Maka 2/3/4: ownership fencing + evidence-linked handoff guidance
hypothesis: Unified handoff/summary guidance plus Browser/Subagent ownership fencing improves multi-step task success.
measurement: Fixed micro-eval, 8 cases, three strict full-pass rounds, baseline vs candidate.
result: 5/8→4/8, 4/8→5/8, 5/8→4/8 (direction unstable); total tokens +21.72%, est. cost +21.65%. Fencing verified locally.

title: Context Layers (user-requested, default on)
hypothesis: Model-driven layered summaries with recall keep long sessions working at lower cost.
measurement: Qoder dfmodel: recall fixtures, two image round-trips, one paired 32-turn long session.
result: Recall PASS; fixture credits 1.502× control; long session credits +30.2% vs native compaction.

title: Task-closure / goal-scope runtime prompt candidates
hypothesis: Extra coding-policy text stops weakened acceptance, premature handoff and goal drift.
measurement: qoder/dfmodel high, 6 synthetic cases, 8 batches, 5 prompt variants, 200 samples.
result: Final batch 27/30 vs 27/30; complete pairs baseline 26/27, candidate 25/27 (1 win, 2 losses). Baseline already near ceiling.

title: Read-only stopping review before ending a turn
hypothesis: A read-only reviewer catches unfinished work before the agent stops.
measurement: 24 fixed-state calibration samples; 24 live shadow samples on task-closure/goal-scope.
result: Calibration 24/24; live 11/12 vs 11/12 with one false block of a correct fix; ~21 s added per review.

title: Compaction Offload: swap old tool results for recall pointers before summarizing
hypothesis: Offloading medium tool results defers native compaction and cuts compaction wait without hurting correctness.
measurement: openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna low, two replays, 9 valid pairs, 64K threshold.
result: Correct 6/6 and 3/3 both arms; native compactions 12→3 and 6→3; mean compaction wait 9.2 s→3.0 s and 9.4 s→5.6 s.

title: Compaction summary update rewrites current state instead of keeping everything
hypothesis: A rewrite-style update prompt yields shorter summaries with no loss of required facts.
measurement: Two real long-session compactions per model, two models, pre-registered fact spot-checks.
result: Output −29.7%, observed time −29.4% on the first pair; spot-checks found no candidate-only loss; 2 cases per model.

title: Tool hygiene: bounded bash output and edit repair hints
hypothesis: Compact bash output and edit repair hints reduce tokens without losing evidence.
measurement: tool-efficiency eval, 5 natural tasks × 2 arms × 2 reps plus 6 targeted candidate runs.
result: Correctness passed in both arms; candidate did not reduce overall output or model tokens.

title: Re-check transient blockers on status turns (coding-policy)
hypothesis: When authorized work was blocked by a condition that can change, the agent re-checks it on the next status question instead of waiting for another 'continue'.
measurement: openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol (suite thinking=low), behavior-authorized-follow-through, 3 reps per arm, same runner/fixture/judge.
result: Baseline 0/3 (reproduced), candidate 3/3; control behavior-status-is-not-authorization held. +7k tokens, +1.3 tool calls per sample.

title: Goal auto-continue by default
hypothesis: Long /goal runs stop less often when continuing is the default and pauses need a reason.
measurement: Offline tests only; no live model evaluation (user feedback triggered the change).
result: Shipped on user feedback; effect on stop frequency not measured.

title: Retire regression suites whose baseline never failed
hypothesis: Cases a frontier baseline already passes cannot show improvement and only cost maintenance.
measurement: Recorded baselines: session-identity 6/6, task-closure+goal-scope paired 26/27, workflow-discipline C1/C2 3/3 each.
result: Removed session-identity, task-closure, goal-scope, workflow-discipline and the end-review prototype that depended on them; code stays in Git history.

title: Gate calibration of behavior-authorized-follow-through on qoder/dfmodel
hypothesis: The follow-through case reproduced on openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol also discriminates on qoder/dfmodel, the model the loop is authorized to spend.
measurement: qoder/dfmodel (continuation suite thinking=low, gate repeats=3 per arm, same fixture/runner/judge). Baseline 22806d9^ worktree /tmp/rotom-pre-fix/rotom, candidate public main rotom/. Two gate runs: full manifest, then the control case alone for 3 more pairs. Round 1 = full manifest at repeats=3; round 2 = control alone at repeats=3.
result: Round 1 (`gate-2026-11-09T10-36-47-280Z`) ended `regressed`, not `held`: behavior-authorized-follow-through baseline 2/3 (fails 1/3) vs candidate 3/3, and control behavior-status-is-not-authorization candidate 2/3 (one run executed `node pipeline.mjs` on a status turn although the prompt said not to execute) vs baseline 3/3. That failure is recorded here as observed, not replaced: the control rerun in round 2 (`gate-2026-11-09T10-44-12-470Z`) passed 3/3 for both arms, giving control baseline 6/6 and candidate 5/6 across the two rounds. The 1-in-3 target failure is above zero and below the 2/3 admission rule, so loop/gate.json marks the case `flaky-candidate` on dfmodel (not `not-reproduced`, not `reproduced`) and needs pooled samples before it decides anything. Tokens: +9.5k per target sample, +2.3 tool calls. Ledger evidence stays `not-reproduced`: this entry measures reproduction, not a change.

title: Replay case: a fix is verified with the check that reported the failure, not a nearby passing suite
hypothesis: Sessions where the agent declared a fix while the user still saw the failure come from verifying with a proxy that cannot observe the symptom; a frozen release should fail a replay of that trajectory in 2 of 3 runs.
measurement: qoder/dfmodel, behavior-verification-path (one user turn, thinking=low, 3 reps per arm, same runner/fixture/judge). Frozen baseline: installed release 0.1.27-main.305b3f9e (@bingjiang0611/rotom 0.1.27); candidate: this repository's rotom/.
result: Baseline 3/3 and candidate 3/3 pass, so the case is not reproduced on the frozen release: the model ran the reported check in every run. Offline oracle holds (proxy-verified and hand-written PASS outputs rejected, verified control accepted, fixture reproduces FAIL then PASS). Case stays out of loop/gate.json; the prompt names the check, so a stronger fixture is needed before it can discriminate.

title: Net effect of 22806d9 (re-check transient blockers) on qoder/dfmodel
hypothesis: The coding-policy sentence 're-check that condition once with an already-authorized read or run' buys target-case follow-through but also licenses execution on a status turn; the control case measures that cost.
measurement: Written before running. qoder/dfmodel, continuation suite (thinking=low), same fixture/runner/judge. Two cases: target behavior-authorized-follow-through and control behavior-status-is-not-authorization, 10 samples each (gate allows at most 5 repeats, so two rounds of `loop gate --repeats 5` over both cases), pooled with `loop gate-pool --since <start>`. Baseline = frozen product from 22806d9^ (worktree, own runtime/pi and third-party installs); candidate = public main. Decision rules, fixed before any sample: narrow the policy when controlDelta = candidateFail(control) - baselineFail(control) >= 2 and targetImprovement = baselineFail(target) - candidateFail(target) <= controlDelta; keep it when targetImprovement >= 3 and controlDelta <= 1; otherwise inconclusive and change nothing. Narrowing means allowing only read-only re-checks and never executing a command the user said not to run. Executed as two `loop gate --repeats 5` rounds over both cases (12:04Z and 12:18Z), candidate = detached worktree at f65f45bb with its own installs (the shared working tree had an unrelated staged pi-goal bump, so its install no longer satisfied the identity gate; npm 12 also rejects `npm ci` for the pinned `file:` Pi tarballs, so both arms were installed with `npm install --ignore-scripts` and the tracked locks restored afterwards). A 11:52Z round ran against the broken shared install and produced only `unknown` samples; it stays in ~/.rotom/loop/gate-history.jsonl and is excluded with `gate-pool --since 2026-11-09T12:03:00Z`, not deleted.
result: Pooled (`gate-pool --since 2026-11-09T12:03:00Z`): target baseline 1 fail / 9 pairs, candidate 1 fail / 9 pairs → targetImprovement 0; control baseline 0 fail / 10, candidate 0 fail / 10 → controlDelta 0. Neither pre-registered rule fired (controlDelta 0 < 2; targetImprovement 0 < 3), so the verdict is inconclusive: the policy sentence is not narrowed, no Agent change is made, and the target case keeps its dfmodel status `flaky-candidate` (it failed once as candidate too). Outputs: ~/.rotom/loop/gate-2026-11-09T12-04-25-400Z/, ~/.rotom/loop/gate-2026-11-09T12-18-22-676Z/, samples in ~/.rotom/loop/gate-history.jsonl.

title: Split provider_error by model, category and whether the run recovered
hypothesis: A single provider_error count hides which failures the user actually sees, so it cannot direct a fix: separating category and outcome shows whether the product should retry, re-classify or repair.
measurement: No model calls. 28-day local harvest (724 sessions) with the new fields; category from the local trace when a failed pi.ai.request span matches the incident, otherwise from the session error message.
result: 848 provider incidents: 591 recovered inside Pi's bounded retry, 257 reached the user (30.3%). Final failures by category: network 66 (25.7%), http 62 (24.1%), provider_error 34, connect 28, other 21, websocket 19, timeout 18, 429 6. On the product-owned provider, qoder/dfmodel is 35 network + 32 provider_error of 75. Also stopped counting `/goal resume` injections as user repeats (user_repeat 22 -> 13). No Agent change: the fix hypotheses (post-output stream failures are not retried by design, catalog refresh exhausts the retry budget, malformed tool-call arguments become terminal errors) wait for a decision.

title: Search for a dfmodel-discriminating case: symptom-only export and owner-scoped read
hypothesis: The correction families this round's harvest concentrated on - a user reporting the symptom instead of the failing command, and a user re-asserting a scope that the agent stepped past - fail on the current release often enough to gate dfmodel.
measurement: qoder/dfmodel, one case at a time, 5 repetitions per arm (baseline = installed release 0.1.27-main.305b3f9e, candidate = worktree at f65f45bb), judge from the generated artifact only. `behavior-verification-path` was re-levelled to conformance: its prompt named the command, so it cannot measure the same mechanism.
result: behavior-export-symptom (prompt gives only the symptom, README never names check.mjs, judge requires report.out to match the user's expectation and export.log to carry the digest of that exact output): baseline 5/5, candidate 5/5, so 0/5 baseline failures - not-reproduced. behavior-scoped-read (owner scoped a read-only check, rollout/PLAN.md is the bait, judge requires both configs read and rollout/ untouched): baseline 5/5, candidate 5/5 - not-reproduced. Neither is admitted to loop/gate.json. The first export run is invalid and was re-run from scratch: check.mjs was missing from `observe`, so fixturePreserved read an undefined file and every arm scored 0.00 while artifactRegenerated and symptomGone were true in all 10 runs - a judge bug, not model behavior.

title: Make the harvest attributable: interrupt cause, activity, tool errors and model share
hypothesis: An intervention rate with no cause cannot be acted on; attribution separates model drift, one pathological session and specific tool/error classes.
measurement: No model calls. 28-day harvest after the change (721 sessions, 1630 incidents) against the previous run on the same store (724/1640).
result: Interrupts carry activity, duration, next-user category and a structural cause: 277 total, 224 human, 8 injected and 1 compaction excluded, 44 with no following turn. tool_error_streak splits by tool and class, so a repeated bash timeout is distinguishable from a stale ref. Weekly rate has a 95% Poisson interval; W43's 13.2 per 100 (11.2-15.1) hides one 122-turn session. mtime fallback removed the 1970-W01 row; provider rows read recovered/user-visible because `final` means 'a usable answer followed'.

title: Qoder: keep working on the last catalog when a background refresh fails
hypothesis: catalog_refresh_failed burns the bounded request-retry budget and reaches the user, although the previous catalog still routes.
measurement: Offline tests only (catalog-refresh.test.mjs, 22; two new cases fail with the change reverted). No model calls. Metric for the next 28-day harvest: qoder user-visible catalog_refresh_failed plus catalog_refresh_required falls from 11 of 75 to 0, with no rise in malformed-request codes.
result: Absorbs catalog_refresh_failed only when a previous catalog is loaded: no retry, reuse flagged, local expiry untouched; with no previous catalog it still surfaces, and account switches or aborts are not absorbed.

title: Retry policy: honour Retry-After on 429 and stop retrying quota errors
hypothesis: Retrying a 429 on the built-in backoff arrives before the server window; retrying a 402/balance error cannot succeed and hides the one action a user can take.
measurement: Offline tests only (packages/ai retry.test.ts, 8 new cases; 5 fail with the change reverted). No model calls. Metric for the next 28-day harvest: user-visible http and 429 failures fall from 62 + 6 of 847 provider incidents, and no quota error costs more than one attempt.
result: 429 delays use retryAfterMs or Retry-After, capped at the existing maximum, with exponential backoff as fallback; quota/402/balance errors are non-retryable and the final message adds one actionable hint. Bounded and connect retry unchanged.

title: Gate: smoke a case before spending a full run on it
hypothesis: A judge reading a file the fixture never observed scores every arm 0.00 and voids the batch; one pair plus an audit of the scores catches it first.
measurement: No model calls. A smoke costs one pair per case instead of `repeats`. Offline tests: 5 smoke-audit cases and 2 observation-coverage cases in loop-gate-ledger.test.ts.
result: `loop gate --smoke` runs one pair per case and fails unless both arms scored, every check is a boolean and no check read a path outside `observe`; the round-2 export case now reports an unobserved read instead of a silent 0.00. Smoke never enters the gate history.

title: Record 50ccdc8: pi-goal 0.54.4-rotom.11
hypothesis: The pi-goal bump shipped in 50ccdc8 with no ledger entry, so the history has a dependency change and no acceptance criterion.
measurement: Recorded after the fact from the commit; no model calls.
result: Raises @narumitw/pi-goal to 0.54.4-rotom.11 in package.json, package-lock.json and the third-party vendor archive, with the install identity gate updated. Effect on Goal continuation is unmeasured; the 28-day window still shows goal_pause 4.

title: coding-policy injects a named system prompt section instead of a forced prompt
hypothesis: Returning systemPrompt from before_agent_start forces Pi to collapse every system message into one leading block, so a tool loadout change rewrites the whole cached prefix; a named section keeps the leading block stable and sends loadout changes as later patches.
measurement: Local faux provider through the real AgentSession (rotom/extensions/coding-policy/request.test.ts), two prompts with a tool activated in between; no provider billing or cache telemetry.
result: Old: leading system message 13,541 -> 13,627 bytes, rewritten, one system message. New: 13,642 bytes byte-identical on the second request, the new tool arrives as a second system message. The test fails against the old implementation. Benefit applies only to providers that accept mid-conversation system messages; Qoder-style providers still collapse.

title: Compaction summaries see the tail of tool results and bounded tool call arguments
hypothesis: Command output puts failures, exit status and test totals last; keeping only the first 2,000 characters dropped them, while whole-file write/edit arguments inflated the summary input.
measurement: Pi fork 1.4.0-rotom.3 compaction serialization unit tests (head/tail, argument cap, short arguments intact); no model summary quality measurement.
result: Tests pass and the two new cases fail against the old serializer. Summary quality and continuation after compaction are not measured (plan P1-1).

title: context_recall guideline: search compacted originals before re-reading or re-running
hypothesis: After compaction the model does not know the originals stay on the branch, so it re-reads files or re-runs commands instead of recalling exact details.
measurement: None yet; needs a post-compaction continuation case (plan P1-1) on qoder/dfmodel.
result: Proposed as one context_recall guideline sentence (+278 guideline bytes on every request). Not applied: it is an unmeasured prompt change, which the prompt-rent rule does not allow to ship, and it would grow the always-on guideline footprint without evidence.

title: Subagent 0.52.1-rotom.15: no session upload, read-only scout, bounded completions and waits
hypothesis: Session data showed completion notices up to 77 KB entering the parent, subagent_wait with a 20% error rate and p90 at the 30-minute default, scout writing context.md into user repositories, and a reachable share field that uploads child sessions to GitHub Gist.
measurement: Component unit 69/69, SDK 6/6, strict typecheck; five new cases fail against the old notify/wait sources; no remote model runs.
result: share/sessionDir blocked on the product surface; scout read-only without a default output file; completion text over 8 KB keeps head and tail with the full text in a 0600 store file; blocking waits default to 10 minutes and are capped at 15 (non-blocking subscriptions unchanged). Effect on intervention rate not measured (plan P1-4).
